title.zh: 卷二十四 唐臣傳第十二: 郭崇韜 安重誨
title.en: Volume 24 Later Tang Biographies 4: Guo Chongtao, An Zhonghui
title.raw: 卷二十四 唐臣傳第十二: 郭崇韜 安重誨 Volume 24 Later Tang Biographies 4: Guo Chongtao, An Zhonghui

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜

translations.literal: Guo Chongtao
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜，代州雁門人也，為河東教練使。

translations.literal: Guo Chongtao was a native of Yanmen in Dai prefecture and served as drill commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao came from Yanmen in Dai prefecture and held the post of Hedong drill commissioner.

sentences.zh: 為人明敏，能應對，以材幹見稱。

translations.literal: As a man he was bright and quick, able in repartee, and famed for talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Bright, quick on his feet, and celebrated for his ability, he was a man who could hold his own in any room.

sentences.zh: 莊宗為晉王，孟知祥為中門使，崇韜為副使。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong was Prince of Jin, Meng Zhixiang was Middle Gate envoy and Chongtao was his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhuangzong still ruled as Prince of Jin, Meng Zhixiang served as Middle Gate envoy with Chongtao as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 中門之職，參管機要，先時，吳珙、張虔厚等皆以中門使相繼獲罪。

translations.literal: The Middle Gate post handled vital secrets; earlier Wu Gong, Zhang Qianhou, and others had served as Middle Gate envoys one after another and all fallen to crime.
translations.idiomatic: Middle Gate envoys touched the realm’s deepest secrets—and Wu Gong, Zhang Qianhou, and others who had held the post before them had fallen to crime, one after another.

sentences.zh: 知祥懼，求外任，莊宗曰：「公欲避事，當舉可代公者。

translations.literal: Zhixiang was afraid and sought an outside post. Zhuangzong said: “If you wish to avoid office, you must recommend someone who can take your place.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang grew fearful and asked for a post outside the capital. Zhuangzong told him: “If you mean to step aside, name someone who can replace you.

sentences.zh: 」知祥乃薦崇韜為中門使，甚見親信。

translations.literal: ” So Zhixiang recommended Chongtao as Middle Gate envoy, and Chongtao won great trust and favor.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhixiang then put forward Chongtao for Middle Gate envoy, and Chongtao soon became one of the prince’s most trusted men.

sentences.zh: 梁王彥章擊破德勝，唐軍東保楊劉，彥章圍之。

translations.literal: Liang’s Wang Yanzhang smashed Desheng; Tang troops withdrew east to Yangliu, and Yanzhang besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanzhang of Liang broke Desheng; the Tang army fell back east to Yangliu, and Yanzhang laid siege.

sentences.zh: 莊宗登壘，望見彥章為重塹以絕唐軍，意輕之，笑曰：「我知其心矣，其欲持久以弊我也。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong climbed the ramparts, saw Yanzhang building heavy trenches to cut off the Tang army, thought lightly of him, and laughed: “I know his mind—he wants a long stand to wear us down.
translations.idiomatic: From the ramparts Zhuangzong watched Yanzhang raise deep trenches to isolate the Tang host and laughed him off: “I see what he wants—a long siege to grind us down.

sentences.zh: 」即引短兵出戰，為彥章伏兵所射，大敗而歸。

translations.literal: ” He led short weapons out to fight, was struck by Yanzhang’s ambush, and returned in great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: ” He took a light force out to fight, walked into Yanzhang’s ambush, and came back in ruin.

sentences.zh: 莊宗問崇韜：「計安出？

translations.literal: Zhuangzong asked Chongtao: “Where does the plan lie?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong turned to Chongtao: “What is our move?

sentences.zh: 」是時，唐已得鄆州矣，崇韜因曰：「彥章圍我於此，其志在取鄆州也。

translations.literal: ” By then Tang had already taken Yan prefecture. Chongtao said: “Yanzhang besieges us here because he wants to take Yan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: ” Tang already held Yan prefecture by then. Chongtao said: “Yanzhang has pinned us here because his real aim is Yan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 臣願得兵數千，據河下流，築壘於必爭之地，以應鄆州為名，彥章必來爭，既分其兵，可以圖也。

translations.literal: I ask for several thousand troops to hold the lower river, build a fort at a place sure to be contested, in the name of supporting Yan prefecture. Yanzhang must come to fight; once his force is divided, we can act.
translations.idiomatic: Give me a few thousand men to seize the lower river, throw up a fort on ground he cannot ignore, and call it support for Yan. He will have to split his army to answer—and then we can strike.

sentences.zh: 然板築之功難卒就，陛下日以精兵挑戰，使彥章兵不得東，十日壘成矣。

translations.literal: But rampart work cannot be finished at once. Your Majesty should daily send crack troops to provoke battle, so Yanzhang’s men cannot move east—in ten days the fort will stand.
translations.idiomatic: Earthworks cannot rise overnight. Send your best troops out each day to keep him fighting here, so his army cannot turn east. In ten days the fort will be done.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗以為然，乃遣崇韜與毛璋將數千人夜行，所過驅掠居人，毀屋伐木，渡河築壘於博州東，晝夜督役，六日壘成。

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong agreed and sent Chongtao with Mao Zhang and several thousand men on a night march. Where they passed they drove and plundered residents, tore down houses and felled timber, crossed the river and built a fort east of Bo prefecture, pressing the work day and night—six days and the fort stood.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong agreed. He sent Chongtao and Mao Zhang with several thousand men on a night march. Everywhere they went they drove off the people, stripped houses for timber, crossed the river, and raised a fort east of Bo prefecture, driving the work without rest—six days, and the walls stood.

sentences.zh: 彥章果引兵急攻之，時方大暑，彥章兵熱死，及攻壘不克，所失太半，還趨楊劉，莊宗迎擊，遂敗之。

translations.literal: Yanzhang indeed led troops in urgent attack. It was deep summer; Yanzhang’s men died of heat. They could not take the fort and lost more than half; they turned back toward Yangliu. Zhuangzong went out to meet them and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang rushed to attack, as Chongtao had foreseen. In the midsummer heat his men dropped dead; they failed to take the fort and lost more than half their strength. As they hurried back toward Yangliu, Zhuangzong met them and broke them.

sentences.zh: 康延孝自梁奔唐，先見崇韜，崇韜延之臥內，盡得梁虛實。

translations.literal: Kang Yanxiao fled from Liang to Tang and first saw Chongtao. Chongtao received him in his inner chamber and learned all of Liang’s strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: When Kang Yanxiao defected from Liang to Tang, his first stop was Chongtao’s quarters. There, in private, he laid bare everything Liang had and lacked.

sentences.zh: 是時，莊宗軍朝城，段凝軍臨河。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuangzong’s army was at Chaocheng and Duan Ning’s army faced the river.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong’s army held Chaocheng while Duan Ning’s Liang force sat on the far bank.

sentences.zh: 唐自失德勝，梁兵日掠澶、相，取黎陽、衛州，而李繼韜以澤潞叛入於梁，契丹數犯幽、涿，又聞延孝言梁方召諸鎮兵欲大舉，唐諸將皆憂惑，以謂成敗未可知。

translations.literal: Since Tang lost Desheng, Liang troops daily raided Chan and Xiang, took Liyang and Weizhou; Li Jitao rebelled with Ze and Lu and went over to Liang; Khitan repeatedly struck You and Zhuo; and hearing Yanxiao say Liang was summoning troops from all circuits for a great campaign—Tang’s generals were anxious and confused, saying success or failure could not be known.
translations.idiomatic: After Desheng fell, Liang raided Chan and Xiang day after day, seized Liyang and Weizhou, and won Li Jitao’s defection with Ze and Lu. Khitan bands kept striking You and Zhuo. Yanxiao brought word that Liang was calling up every circuit for a major push. Tang’s commanders grew fearful and uncertain, muttering that the outcome was anyone’s guess.

sentences.zh: 莊宗患之，以問諸將，諸將皆曰：「唐得鄆州，隔河難守，不若棄鄆與梁，而西取衛州、黎陽，以河為界，與梁約罷兵，毋相攻，庶幾以為後圖。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was troubled and asked his generals. All said: “Tang holds Yan prefecture across the river and cannot defend it. Better abandon Yan to Liang, take Weizhou and Liyang to the west, and make the river the boundary. Make a truce with Liang—no mutual attack—and perhaps leave room for later plans.
translations.idiomatic: Distressed, Zhuangzong polled his generals. All of them said: “Yan prefecture sits on the wrong side of the river—we cannot hold it. Give Yan back to Liang, take Weizhou and Liyang to the west, and treat the river as the border. Call a truce and buy time for a later move.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗不悅，退臥帳中，召崇韜問計，崇韜曰：「陛下興兵仗義，將士疲戰爭、生民苦轉餉者，十餘年矣。

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong was displeased, withdrew to lie in his tent, and called Chongtao for counsel. Chongtao said: “Your Majesty raised the army in righteousness. For more than ten years soldiers have grown weary of war and the people have suffered under transport levies.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong would not hear it. He withdrew to his tent and sent for Chongtao. Chongtao said: “Your Majesty took up arms in a just cause. For more than ten years your soldiers have known nothing but battle, and the people have groaned under supply levies.

sentences.zh: 況今大號已建，自河以北，人皆引首以望成功而思休息。

translations.literal: Moreover the great title is now established—from north of the river everyone lifts his head to gaze toward success and longs for rest.
translations.idiomatic: You have already claimed the imperial title. North of the river, every man looks up waiting for victory—and for peace.

sentences.zh: 今得一鄆州，不能守而棄之，雖欲指河為界，誰為陛下守之？

translations.literal: Now that we have Yan prefecture, if we cannot hold it and abandon it—even if we mean to make the river the boundary, who will guard it for Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: We have just taken Yan prefecture. If we cannot keep it and throw it away, who will hold the river line for you?

sentences.zh: 且唐未失德勝時，四方商賈，征輸必集，薪芻糧餉，其積如山。

translations.literal: Moreover when Tang had not lost Desheng, merchants from all quarters and transport levies all gathered—firewood, fodder, grain and rations piled like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Before Desheng fell, merchants and convoys poured in from every direction—firewood, fodder, grain, and pay stacked like hills.

sentences.zh: 自失南城，保楊劉，道路轉徙，耗亡太半。

translations.literal: Since losing the southern city and holding Yangliu, goods have been moved along the roads and more than half has been lost.
translations.idiomatic: Since we lost the southern city and fell back to Yangliu, everything we move along the roads loses more than half on the way.

sentences.zh: 而魏、博五州，秋稼不稔，竭民而斂，不支數月，此豈按兵持久之時乎？

translations.literal: Yet in the five prefectures of Wei and Bo the autumn crop did not ripen—exhausting the people to levy, we cannot last several months. Is this a time to hold the army and endure?
translations.idiomatic: In Wei and Bo’s five prefectures the autumn harvest failed. We are squeezing the people dry and cannot feed the army for another few months. This is no moment to sit and wait.

sentences.zh: 臣自康延孝來，盡得梁之虛實，此真天亡之時也。

translations.literal: Since Yanxiao came I have learned all of Liang’s condition. This is truly Heaven’s hour for their destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yanxiao arrived I have learned Liang inside out. Heaven itself is handing us their ruin.

sentences.zh: 願陛下分兵守魏，固楊劉，而自鄆長驅搗其巢穴，不出半月，天下定矣！

translations.literal: I ask Your Majesty to divide troops to hold Wei, fortify Yangliu, and from Yan drive straight at their nest—not half a month and the realm will be settled!
translations.idiomatic: Leave a force to hold Wei, lock down Yangliu, and from Yan ride straight into their heartland. In less than half a month the realm will be yours!

sentences.zh: 」莊宗大喜曰：「此大丈夫之事也！

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong was greatly delighted: “This is the affair of a true man!
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong brightened: “Now that is a man’s counsel!

sentences.zh: 」因問司天，司天言：「歲不利用兵。

translations.literal: ” He then asked the Director of Astronomy, who said: “This year is ill-suited for war.
translations.idiomatic: ” He consulted the Director of Astronomy, who answered: “The stars say this is no year for war.

sentences.zh: 」崇韜曰：「古者命將，鑿兇門而出。

translations.literal: ” Chongtao said: “In antiquity when emperors commissioned generals they broke through the Gate of Ill Omen to send them out.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chongtao said: “Ancient emperors broke through the Gate of Ill Omen when they sent generals to war.

sentences.zh: 況成算已決，區區常談，豈足信也！

translations.literal: Moreover the winning plan is already settled—how can petty common talk be trusted!
translations.idiomatic: The winning plan is already in hand—why trust idle chatter from the calendar!

sentences.zh: 」莊宗即日下令軍中，歸其家屬於魏，夜渡楊劉，從鄆州入襲汴，八日而滅梁。

translations.literal: ” That very day Zhuangzong ordered the army to send families back to Wei, crossed Yangliu by night, entered from Yan prefecture to strike Bian—and in eight days Liang was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: ” That same day Zhuangzong sent the army’s families back to Wei, crossed Yangliu by night, swept in from Yan toward Bian—and in eight days Liang was gone.

sentences.zh: 莊宗推功，賜崇韜鐵券，拜侍中、成德軍節度使，依前樞密使。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong credited his merit, granted Chongtao an iron certificate, appointed him Palace Secretary and military governor of Chengde Circuit, and kept him as before as Privy Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong rewarded him with an iron certificate of mercy, made him Palace Secretary and military governor of Chengde Circuit, and kept him on as Privy Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 莊宗與諸將以兵取天下，而崇韜未嘗居戰陣，徒以謀議居佐命第一之功，位兼將相，遂以天下為己任，遇事無所回避。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong and the generals took the realm by arms, yet Chongtao had never stood in the battle line—he held first merit among those who aided the founding solely through counsel. His rank joined general and minister; he then took the realm as his own charge and met affairs without evasion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong and his generals had won the realm with swords, but Chongtao had never once stood in the battle line. By counsel alone he ranked first among the founders. General and minister in one man, he took the empire as his own burden and never shrank from a hard decision.

sentences.zh: 而宦官、伶人用事，特不便也。

translations.literal: But eunuchs and actors held power—this was especially inconvenient to him.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs and actors held the levers of power—and that sat ill with him.

sentences.zh: 初，崇韜與宦者馬紹宏俱為中門使，而紹宏位在上。

translations.literal: At first Chongtao and the eunuch Ma Shaohong were both Middle Gate envoys, and Shaohong’s rank was above his.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Chongtao and the eunuch Ma Shaohong had both served as Middle Gate envoys, with Shaohong senior to him.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗即位，二人當為樞密使，而崇韜不欲紹宏在己上，乃以張居翰為樞密使，紹宏為宣徽使。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne both should have become Privy Commissioners, but Chongtao did not want Shaohong above him—so Zhang Juchang was made Privy Commissioner and Shaohong Commissioner of the Court of Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took the throne both men were due for Privy Commissioner. Chongtao refused to serve beneath Shaohong, so Zhang Juchang became Privy Commissioner while Shaohong was made Commissioner of the Court of Palace Attendants.

sentences.zh: 紹宏失職怨望，崇韜因置內勾使，以紹宏領之。

translations.literal: Shaohong, losing his post, nursed resentment. Chongtao therefore created the Internal Audit Commissioner and put Shaohong in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of real power, Shaohong seethed. Chongtao answered by inventing the post of Internal Audit Commissioner and handing it to him.

sentences.zh: 凡天下錢谷出入於租庸者，皆經內勾。

translations.literal: All revenues and expenditures of the realm in tax and labor service funds passed through Internal Audit.
translations.idiomatic: Every coin of tax and labor revenue that moved through the empire now passed through Internal Audit.

sentences.zh: 既而文簿繁多，州縣為弊，遽罷其事，而紹宏尤側目。

translations.literal: Soon records multiplied and prefectures and counties suffered; the office was abruptly abolished—and Shaohong glared all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Paperwork soon buried the prefectures and counties. The office was killed off almost as quickly as it was born—and Shaohong’s hatred only deepened.

sentences.zh: 崇韜頗懼，語其故人子弟曰：「吾佐天子取天下，今大功已就，而群小交興，吾欲避之，歸守鎮陽，庶幾免禍，可乎？

translations.literal: Chongtao grew quite afraid and told the sons of old friends: “I aided the Son of Heaven in taking the realm. Now the great work is done and petty men rise together. I wish to withdraw, return to guard Zhenyuan, and perhaps escape disaster—is that possible?
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao grew afraid and confided in the sons of old friends: “I helped the emperor win the realm. The great work is done, and petty men are closing in. I want to withdraw to Zhenyuan and try to dodge ruin—is that wise?

sentences.zh: 」故人子弟對曰：「俚語曰：『騎虎者，勢不得下。

translations.literal: ” The sons of old friends replied: “A folk saying goes: ‘He who rides a tiger cannot easily dismount.’
translations.idiomatic: ” They answered: “There is a saying: ‘Once you ride the tiger, you cannot climb down.’

sentences.zh: 』今公權位已隆，而下多怨嫉，一失其勢，能自安乎？

translations.literal: ’ Your rank and power are already exalted, and many below bear jealousy—once you lose that power, can you keep yourself safe?
translations.idiomatic: ’ Your rank is already towering and envy runs deep below. Lose your grip on power, and who will keep you safe?

sentences.zh: 」崇韜曰：「奈何？

translations.literal: ” Chongtao said: “What then?
translations.idiomatic: ” Chongtao asked: “Then what should I do?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「今中宮未立，而劉氏有寵，宜請立劉氏為皇后，而多建天下利害以便民者，然後退而乞身。

translations.literal: ” They answered: “The empress is not yet established, yet the Liu consort enjoys favor. You should ask that Lady Liu be made empress, propose many measures of public benefit to ease the people, and then withdraw and request release from office.
translations.idiomatic: ” They said: “The empress has not been enthroned, yet Lady Liu already holds the emperor’s heart. Ask that she be made empress. Push reforms that help the people. Then ask to retire.

sentences.zh: 天子以公有大功而無過，必不聽公去。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, seeing your great merit and no fault, will surely not let you go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor will see your great service and refuse to let you leave.

sentences.zh: 是外有避權之名，而內有中宮之助，又為天下所悅，雖有讒間，其可動乎？

translations.literal: Then outwardly you have the name of yielding power, inwardly the empress’s aid, and the realm’s goodwill besides—even if slander comes, can it move you?
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly you will look modest; inwardly the empress will stand with you; the people will be on your side. Even if slander comes, who will be able to touch you?

sentences.zh: 」崇韜以為然，乃上書請立劉氏為皇后。

translations.literal: ” Chongtao thought it sound and memorialized asking that Lady Liu be made empress.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chongtao took the advice and memorialized to make Lady Liu empress.

sentences.zh: 崇韜素廉，自從入洛，始受四方賂遺，故人子弟或以為言，崇韜曰：「吾位兼將相，祿賜巨萬，豈少此邪？

translations.literal: Chongtao had always been frugal; only after entering Luoyang did he begin accepting gifts from all quarters. Sons of old friends sometimes remarked on it. Chongtao said: “My rank joins general and minister; salary and gifts reach tens of thousands—would I lack this?
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao had always lived cleanly. Only after entering Luoyang did he begin taking gifts from every quarter. When old friends’ sons questioned it, he said: “I hold general and minister in one body and draw pay in the tens of thousands—do I need this?

sentences.zh: 今藩鎮諸侯，多梁舊將，皆主上斬袪射鉤之人也。

translations.literal: Now the feudal lords are mostly Liang’s old generals—all men the sovereign once spared at the belt or forgave though they served his enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the frontier lords are Liang’s old commanders—men Your Majesty once spared though they had worn the enemy’s colors.

sentences.zh: 今一切拒之，豈無反側？

translations.literal: If I reject them all, will there not be unrest?
translations.idiomatic: Turn every gift away cold, and how long before they turn on us?

sentences.zh: 且藏於私家，何異公帑？

translations.literal: Besides, if it stays in private hands, how is it different from the public treasury?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, what I hold in my house is no different from what sits in the treasury.

sentences.zh: 」明年，天子有事南郊，乃悉獻其所藏，以佐賞給。

translations.literal: ” The next year when the Son of Heaven performed the southern-suburb rite, Chongtao presented all he had stored to aid rewards and grants.
translations.idiomatic: ” The next year, when the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb, Chongtao turned over everything he had kept to help pay the court’s rewards.

sentences.zh: 莊宗已郊，遂立劉氏為皇后。

translations.literal: After Zhuangzong had sacrificed at the suburbs, Lady Liu was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: After the suburban rites Zhuangzong enthroned Lady Liu as empress.

sentences.zh: 崇韜累表自陳，請依唐舊制，還樞密使於內臣，而並辭鎮陽，優詔不允。

translations.literal: Chongtao repeatedly memorialized on his own behalf, asking to restore the Tang custom of returning the Privy Commission to inner courtiers, and at the same time declined Zhenyuan—a gracious edict would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao memorialized again and again, asking to restore the old Tang practice of putting eunuchs back in the Privy Commission and to be released from Zhenyuan. The court answered with a gracious refusal.

sentences.zh: 崇韜又曰：「臣從陛下軍朝城，定計破梁，陛下撫臣背而約曰：『事了，與卿一鎮。

translations.literal: Chongtao again said: “When I followed Your Majesty’s army at Chaocheng and we settled the plan to break Liang, Your Majesty patted my back and pledged: ‘When it is done, I give you a circuit.’
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao pressed on: “At Chaocheng, when we fixed the plan to destroy Liang, Your Majesty clapped my back and promised: ‘When this is over, you get a circuit.’

sentences.zh: 』今天下一家，俊賢並進，臣憊矣，願乞身如約。

translations.literal: ’ Now the realm is one house; worthy men advance together. I am weary and ask release as pledged.
translations.idiomatic: ’ The realm is united now and talent fills the court. I am spent, and I ask to retire as you promised.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗召崇韜謂曰：「朝城之約，許卿一鎮，不許卿去。

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong summoned Chongtao and said: “The Chaocheng pledge grants you a circuit—it does not grant you departure.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong called Chongtao in and said: “At Chaocheng I promised you a circuit—not your freedom.

sentences.zh: 欲舍朕，安之乎？

translations.literal: You would leave me—where would you go?
translations.idiomatic: You would leave me—where else would you go?

sentences.zh: 」崇韜因建天下利害二十五事，施行之。

translations.literal: ” Chongtao then proposed twenty-five measures of public benefit for the realm, and they were enacted.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chongtao answered by drafting twenty-five reforms for the public good, and Zhuangzong put them into effect.

sentences.zh: 李嗣源為成德軍節度使，徙崇韜忠武。

translations.literal: Li Siyuan was military governor of Chengde Circuit; Chongtao was moved to Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan took Chengde Circuit; Chongtao was transferred to Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 崇韜因自陳權位已極，言甚懇至。

translations.literal: Chongtao then declared on his own behalf that his power and rank had reached their limit—his words were very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao pleaded again that he had risen as high as any man should—his words were almost a confession.

sentences.zh: 莊宗曰：「豈可朕居天下之尊，使卿無尺寸之地？

translations.literal: Zhuangzong said: “How can I, seated in the realm’s highest honor, leave you without even a patch of ground?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong said: “How can I sit as emperor and leave you without even a corner of earth to call your own?

sentences.zh: 」崇韜辭不已，遂罷其命，仍為侍中、樞密使。

translations.literal: ” Chongtao declined without cease, so the appointment was withdrawn; he remained Palace Secretary and Privy Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chongtao would not stop refusing, so Zhuangzong canceled the transfer and kept him as Palace Secretary and Privy Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 同光三年夏，霖雨不止，大水害民田，民多流死。

translations.literal: In summer of the third year of Tongguang rains did not cease; great floods ruined the people’s fields and many drowned in flight.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Tongguang year three the rains would not stop. Floods swallowed the fields and refugees drowned by the thousands.

sentences.zh: 莊宗患宮中暑濕不可居，思得高樓避暑。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong fretted that the palace was damp and stifling in summer and wished for a high tower to escape the heat.
translations.idiomatic: The palace grew muggy and unbearable, and Zhuangzong began to dream of a tall tower where he could breathe.

sentences.zh: 宦官進曰：「臣見長安全盛時，大明、興慶宮樓閣百數。

translations.literal: Eunuchs stepped forward: “Your servant saw Chang’an at its height—the palaces of Daming and Xingqing had towers and pavilions in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs whispered: “We remember Chang’an in its glory—Daming and Xingqing alone held towers and halls by the hundred.

sentences.zh: 今大內不及故時卿相家。

translations.literal: Now the inner palace does not match the homes of ministers in those days.
translations.idiomatic: Today the inner palace is poorer than a great minister’s house in Tang times.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗曰：「吾富有天下，豈不能作一樓？

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong said: “I possess the wealth of the realm—can I not build one tower?
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong said: “I own the wealth of the empire—surely I can raise one tower.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣宮苑使王允平營之。

translations.literal: ” He sent the Palace Parks commissioner Wang Yunping to undertake it.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent Wang Yunping, commissioner of the Palace Parks, to build it.

sentences.zh: 宦官曰：「郭崇韜眉頭不伸，常為租庸惜財用，陛下雖欲有作，其可得乎？

translations.literal: Eunuchs said: “Guo Chongtao’s brow never unknits—he always pinches tax revenues. Even if Your Majesty wishes to build, can it be done?
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs added: “Guo Chongtao’s brow is always furrowed. He hoards every coin of tax revenue. Even if Your Majesty wants a tower, will Chongtao allow it?

sentences.zh: 」莊宗乃使人問崇韜曰：「昔吾與梁對壘於河上，雖祁寒盛暑，被甲跨馬，不以為勞。

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong then sent someone to ask Chongtao: “Once I faced Liang across the river—bitter cold or blazing heat, armored and on horseback, I never called it hardship.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong sent a messenger to Chongtao: “On the river line against Liang I wore armor in freezing cold and brutal heat and never complained.

sentences.zh: 今居深宮，蔭廣廈，不勝其熱，何也？

translations.literal: Now I dwell deep in the palace, shaded by broad halls, yet cannot bear the heat—why?
translations.idiomatic: Now I live deep in the palace under wide roofs and cannot stand the heat—why?

sentences.zh: 」崇韜對曰：「陛下昔以天下為心，今以一身為意，艱難逸豫，為慮不同，其勢自然也。

translations.literal: ” Chongtao answered: “Your Majesty once held the realm in heart; now you hold yourself alone in mind. Hardship and ease call for different concerns—the situation makes it natural.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chongtao answered: “Then Your Majesty’s heart held the whole realm; now it holds only yourself. Hardship and comfort ask different things of a man—that is only natural.

sentences.zh: 願陛下無忘創業之難，常如河上，則可使繁暑坐變清涼。

translations.literal: I ask Your Majesty not to forget the hardship of founding the enterprise—as on the river—and then even fierce summer heat will turn to coolness where you sit.
translations.idiomatic: Do not forget the struggle of founding the dynasty. Keep the spirit you had on the river, and even this fierce summer will feel cool where you sit.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗默然。

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong was silent.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong said nothing.

sentences.zh: 終遣允平起樓，崇韜果切諫。

translations.literal: In the end he still sent Yunping to raise the tower; Chongtao indeed remonstrated sharply.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Zhuangzong still ordered Yunping to build—and Chongtao remonstrated as fiercely as he had warned.

sentences.zh: 宦官曰：「崇韜之第，無異皇居，安知陛下之熱！

translations.literal: Eunuchs said: “Chongtao’s mansion is no different from the imperial residence—how would he know Your Majesty’s heat!
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs hissed: “Chongtao’s own house is fit for an emperor—what does he know of Your Majesty’s suffering in the heat!

sentences.zh: 」由是讒間愈入。

translations.literal: ” From this slander entered ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: ” From that day the whispers against him only grew louder.

sentences.zh: 河南縣令羅貫，為人強直，頗為崇韜所知。

translations.literal: Luo Guan, magistrate of Henan county, was by nature forceful and upright and was well regarded by Chongtao.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Guan, magistrate of Henan county, was hard and straight by nature, and Chongtao thought highly of him.

sentences.zh: 貫正身奉法，不受權豪請托，宦官、伶人有所求請，書積几案，一不以報，皆以示崇韜。

translations.literal: Guan conducted himself by law and accepted no requests from powerful families. When eunuchs and actors sought favors, letters piled on his desk and he answered none—he showed them all to Chongtao.
translations.idiomatic: Guan lived by the law and took no favors from the powerful. When eunuchs and actors wrote asking for special treatment, their letters stacked on his desk unanswered—and he showed every one to Chongtao.

sentences.zh: 崇韜數以為言，宦官、伶人由此切齒。

translations.literal: Chongtao spoke of this repeatedly; eunuchs and actors gnashed their teeth because of it.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao kept raising the matter at court. The eunuchs and actors hated him for it.

sentences.zh: 河南自故唐時張全義為尹，縣令多出其門，全義廝養畜之。

translations.literal: Henan since old Tang days, when Zhang Quanyi was prefect, had magistrates mostly from his household—Quanyi raised and kept them like retainers.
translations.idiomatic: In the old Tang days Zhang Quanyi had governed Henan, and most county magistrates had come from his household—men he had raised like private retainers.

sentences.zh: 及貫為之，奉全義不屈，縣民恃全義為不法者，皆按誅之。

translations.literal: When Guan held the post he would not bow to Quanyi; county people who relied on Quanyi to break the law—Guan investigated and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Guan would not defer to Quanyi. County people who had counted on Quanyi’s protection to break the law—Guan investigated them and had them put to death.

sentences.zh: 全義大怒，嘗使人告劉皇后，從容為白貫事，而左右日夜共攻其短。

translations.literal: Quanyi was greatly angered and once sent men to tell Empress Liu, gently pleading Guan’s case—but the emperor’s attendants day and night jointly attacked Guan’s faults.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi was furious and sent men to Empress Liu to plead Guan’s case in soft words. Meanwhile the emperor’s attendants spent day and night picking at Guan’s every flaw.

sentences.zh: 莊宗未有以發。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong had no pretext to act.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong still lacked a pretext to move against him.

sentences.zh: 皇太后崩，葬坤陵，陵在壽安，莊宗幸陵作所，而道路泥塗，橋壞。

translations.literal: The empress dowager died and was buried at Kun tomb in Shou’an. Zhuangzong went to the tomb works, but the roads were mud and the bridges broken.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager died she was buried at Kun tomb in Shou’an. Zhuangzong went to oversee the work, but the roads had turned to mud and the bridges had collapsed.

sentences.zh: 莊宗止輿問：「誰主者？

translations.literal: Zhuangzong halted his carriage and asked: “Who is in charge?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong stopped his carriage and demanded: “Who is responsible for this?

sentences.zh: 」宦官曰：「屬河南。

translations.literal: ” Eunuchs said: “It falls to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: ” The eunuchs said: “That is Henan’s jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 」因亟召貫，貫至，對曰：「臣初不奉詔，請詰主者。

translations.literal: ” Guan was urgently summoned. When he arrived he replied: “Your servant was never given the edict—please question whoever is in charge.
translations.idiomatic: ” Guan was summoned at once. When he came he answered: “I never received the edict for this work—Your Majesty should ask whoever was put in charge.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗曰：「爾之所部，復問何人！

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong said: “It is your jurisdiction—whom else would I ask!
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong snapped: “It is your county—whom else should I ask!

sentences.zh: 」即下貫獄，獄吏榜掠，體無完膚。

translations.literal: ” Guan was thrown into prison; jailers beat and flayed him until no patch of skin was whole.
translations.idiomatic: ” Guan was thrown into jail. The jailers beat him until not an inch of skin was left whole.

sentences.zh: 明日，傳詔殺之。

translations.literal: The next day an edict was transmitted ordering his execution.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict went out ordering his death.

sentences.zh: 崇韜諫曰：「貫罪無佗，橋道不修，法不當死。

translations.literal: Chongtao remonstrated: “Guan’s crime is nothing else—roads and bridges not repaired. By law he should not die.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao remonstrated: “Guan’s only fault is failing to repair the roads and bridges. By law that is not a capital crime.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗怒曰：「太后靈駕將發，天子車輿往來，橋道不修，卿言無罪，是朋黨也！

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong raged: “The empress dowager’s coffin is about to depart; the Son of Heaven’s carriage goes back and forth—roads and bridges unrepaired, and you say he is guiltless? That is faction!
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong raged: “The empress dowager’s coffin is about to leave! The emperor’s carriage must pass here again and again—and you say an unrepaired road is no crime? You are shielding him!

sentences.zh: 」崇韜曰：「貫雖有罪，當具獄行法於有司。

translations.literal: ” Chongtao said: “Though Guan has guilt, there should be a full dossier and law applied through the proper offices.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chongtao said: “Even if Guan is guilty, there should be a proper trial and sentence through the legal offices.

sentences.zh: 陛下以萬乘之尊，怒一縣令，使天下之人，言陛下用法不公，臣等之過也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, with the honor of ten thousand chariots, raging at one county magistrate—making all under Heaven say you apply law unfairly—is our fault as ministers.
translations.idiomatic: For the Son of Heaven to vent his wrath on one county magistrate and let the realm say justice is uneven—that is our failure as your ministers.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗曰：「貫，公所愛，任公裁決！

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong said: “Guan is one you favor—you decide!
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong said: “Guan is your man—then you judge him!

sentences.zh: 」因起入宮，崇韜隨之，論不已。

translations.literal: ” He rose and entered the palace; Chongtao followed, arguing without cease.
translations.idiomatic: ” He stood and went inside. Chongtao followed him, pleading without stop.

sentences.zh: 莊宗自闔殿門，崇韜不得入。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong closed the palace gate himself; Chongtao could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong shut the palace gate himself; Chongtao could not follow him in.

sentences.zh: 貫卒見殺。

translations.literal: Guan was at last killed.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was killed in the end.

sentences.zh: 明年征蜀，議擇大將。

translations.literal: The next year they marched against Shu and debated choosing a chief general.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they marched against Shu and debated who should lead.

sentences.zh: 時明宗為總管，當行。

translations.literal: At that time Mingzong was overall commander and ought to go.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong was then overall commander and was the man who ought to go.

sentences.zh: 而崇韜以讒見危，思立大功為自安之計，乃曰：「契丹為患北邊，非總管不可禦。

translations.literal: But Chongtao, endangered by slander, thought to secure himself with a great feat and said: “The Khitan trouble the northern frontier; only the overall commander can repel them.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao, endangered by slander, sought a great victory to save himself and said: “The Khitan threaten the north—only the overall commander can hold them.

sentences.zh: 魏王繼岌，國之儲副，而大功未立，且親王為元帥，唐故事也。

translations.literal: Prince Jiji is the heir, yet he has won no great merit; moreover, an imperial prince as commander-in-chief is Tang custom.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jiji is the heir, yet he has won no great deed; and an imperial prince as field marshal is Tang custom.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗曰：「繼岌，小子，豈任大事？

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong said: “Jiji is a boy—can he bear so great a charge?
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong said: “Jiji is a boy—can he bear so great a burden?

sentences.zh: 必為我擇其副。

translations.literal: You must choose his deputy for me.
translations.idiomatic: Choose his deputy for me.

sentences.zh: 」崇韜未及言，莊宗曰：「吾得之矣，無以易卿也。

translations.literal: Before Chongtao could speak, Zhuangzong said: “I have my man—none can replace you.
translations.idiomatic: Before Chongtao could answer, Zhuangzong said: “I have my man—none can replace you.

sentences.zh: 」乃以繼岌為西南面行營都統，崇韜為招討使，軍政皆決崇韜。

translations.literal: ” He then made Jiji overall commander for the southwest campaign and Chongtao pacification commissioner; all military and political decisions rested with Chongtao.
translations.idiomatic: ” He made Jiji overall commander for the southwest campaign and Chongtao pacification commissioner; military and civil affairs alike rested with Chongtao.

sentences.zh: 唐軍入蜀，所過迎降。

translations.literal: Tang troops entered Shu; wherever they passed, cities surrendered in welcome.
translations.idiomatic: Tang troops entered Shu; wherever they marched, cities came out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 王衍弟宗弼，陰送款於崇韜，求為西川兵馬留後，崇韜以節度使許之。

translations.literal: Wang Yan’s brother Zongbi secretly sent terms to Chongtao, asking to be kept-on military commissioner of Xichuan; Chongtao promised him the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan’s brother Zongbi secretly sent terms to Chongtao, asking to be kept on as Xichuan military commissioner; Chongtao promised him the circuit.

sentences.zh: 軍至成都，宗弼遷衍於西宮，悉取衍嬪妓、珍寶奉崇韜及其子廷誨。

translations.literal: When the army reached Chengdu, Zongbi moved Yan to the western palace and gathered Yan’s concubines, entertainers, and treasures to present to Chongtao and his son Yanhui.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Chengdu, Zongbi moved Yan to the western palace and sent Yan’s concubines, entertainers, and treasures to Chongtao and his son Yanhui.

sentences.zh: 又與蜀人列狀見魏王，請崇韜留鎮蜀。

translations.literal: Shu men also filed a petition to the Prince of Wei asking Chongtao to remain and govern Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Shu men also petitioned the Prince of Wei to keep Chongtao in command of Shu.

sentences.zh: 繼岌頗疑崇韜，崇韜無以自明，因以事斬宗弼及其弟宗渥、宗勛，沒其家財。

translations.literal: Jiji grew quite suspicious of Chongtao; Chongtao could not clear himself and therefore had Zongbi and his brothers Zongwo and Zongxun executed and their property confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji grew deeply suspicious of Chongtao. Unable to clear himself, Chongtao seized on a pretext to execute Zongbi and his brothers Zongwo and Zongxun and confiscate their property.

sentences.zh: 蜀人大恐。

translations.literal: The people of Shu were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu were terrified.

sentences.zh: 崇韜素嫉宦官，嘗謂繼岌曰：「王有破蜀功，師旋，必為太子，俟主上千秋萬歲後，當盡去宦官，至於扇馬，亦不可騎。

translations.literal: Chongtao had always despised the eunuchs. He once told Jiji: “You have the merit of breaking Shu. When the army returns you will surely be made crown prince; after our lord’s passing you should expel all the eunuchs—even the grooms who fan the horses should not be allowed to ride.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao had always despised the eunuchs. He once told Jiji: “You broke Shu. When the army returns you will surely be made crown prince; after our lord’s death you should drive out every eunuch—even the grooms who fan the horses should not ride.

sentences.zh: 」繼岌監軍李從襲等見崇韜專任軍事，心已不平，及聞此言，遂皆切齒，思有以圖之。

translations.literal: Jiji’s army supervisors Li Congxi and the others, already resentful that Chongtao monopolized military affairs, heard this and gnashed their teeth, seeking a way to destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji’s army supervisors Li Congxi and the others, already angry that Chongtao monopolized military affairs, heard this and gnashed their teeth, plotting to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 莊宗聞破蜀，遣宦官向延嗣勞軍，崇韜不郊迎，延嗣大怒，因與從襲等共構之。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong heard Shu was broken, he sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to reward the army; Chongtao did not go out to greet him at the suburbs; Yansi flew into a rage and joined with Congxi and the others in plotting against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong heard Shu had fallen, he sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to reward the army. Chongtao did not go out to greet him at the suburbs. Yansi raged and joined Congxi and the others in plotting against him.

sentences.zh: 延嗣還，上蜀簿，得兵三十萬，馬九千五百匹，兵器七百萬，糧二百五十三萬石，錢一百九十二萬緡，金銀二十二萬兩，珠玉犀象二萬，文錦綾羅五十萬匹。

translations.literal: When Yansi returned he submitted the Shu inventory: three hundred thousand troops, nine thousand five hundred horses, seven million weapons, two million five hundred thirty thousand shi of grain, one million nine hundred twenty thousand strings of cash, two hundred twenty thousand liang of gold and silver, twenty thousand pearls, jade, rhinoceros horn, and ivory, five hundred thousand bolts of patterned silk and damask.
translations.idiomatic: Yansi returned and submitted the Shu inventory: three hundred thousand troops, nine thousand five hundred horses, seven million weapons, two million five hundred thirty thousand shi of grain, one million nine hundred twenty thousand strings of cash, two hundred twenty thousand liang of gold and silver, twenty thousand pearls, jade, rhinoceros horn, and ivory, and five hundred thousand bolts of patterned silk and damask.

sentences.zh: 莊宗曰：「人言蜀天下之富國也，所得止於此邪？

translations.literal: Zhuangzong said: “Men say Shu is the richest kingdom under heaven—is this all there is?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong said: “Men call Shu the richest kingdom under heaven—is this all there is?

sentences.zh: 」延嗣因言蜀之寶貨皆入崇韜，且誣其有異志，將危魏王。

translations.literal: Yansi then said all Shu’s treasure had gone into Chongtao’s hands and slandered him as disloyal, plotting to endanger the Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yansi then said all Shu’s treasure had gone to Chongtao and accused him of disloyalty, plotting to endanger the Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 莊宗怒，遣宦官馬彥珪至蜀，視崇韜去就。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong raged and sent the eunuch Ma Yan’gui to Shu to observe what Chongtao intended.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong raged and sent the eunuch Ma Yan’gui to Shu to see what Chongtao meant to do.

sentences.zh: 彥珪以告劉皇后，劉皇后教彥珪矯詔魏王殺之。

translations.literal: Yan’gui told Empress Liu; Empress Liu instructed Yan’gui to forge an edict ordering the Prince of Wei to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan’gui told Empress Liu, and she told him to forge an edict ordering the Prince of Wei to kill Chongtao.

sentences.zh: 崇韜有子五人，其二從死於蜀，餘皆見殺。

translations.literal: Chongtao had five sons; two died with him in Shu, the rest were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao had five sons; two died with him in Shu, and the rest were killed.

sentences.zh: 其破蜀所得，皆籍沒。

translations.literal: All that he had taken in the conquest of Shu was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: All he had taken in the conquest of Shu was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，詔許歸葬，以其太原故宅賜其二孫。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he issued an edict allowing burial and granted his two grandsons his old Taiyuan residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne he allowed Chongtao burial and granted his two grandsons his old Taiyuan residence.

sentences.zh: 當崇韜用事，自宰相豆盧革、韋悅等皆傾附之，崇韜父諱弘，革等即因佗事，奏改弘文館為崇文館。

translations.literal: While Chongtao held power, even grand councilors Doulu Ge and Wei Yue leaned toward him; Chongtao’s father’s taboo name was Hong; Ge and the others seized on some other business to memorialize renaming Hongwen Hall as Chongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: While Chongtao held power, even grand councilors Doulu Ge and Wei Yue fawned on him. Chongtao’s father’s taboo name was Hong; Ge and the others seized on some other matter and memorialized to rename Hongwen Hall as Chongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 以其姓郭，因以為子儀之後，崇韜遂以為然。

translations.literal: Because his surname was Guo they claimed him as a descendant of Guo Ziyi; Chongtao came to believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Because his surname was Guo they claimed him as Guo Ziyi’s descendant; Chongtao came to believe it.

sentences.zh: 其伐蜀也，過子儀墓，下馬號慟而去，聞者頗以為笑。

translations.literal: On the Shu campaign he passed Ziyi’s tomb, dismounted, wailed bitterly, and went on; those who heard of it mostly laughed.
translations.idiomatic: On the Shu campaign he passed Ziyi’s tomb, dismounted, wailed bitterly, and went on; those who heard of it mostly laughed.

sentences.zh: 然崇韜盡忠國家，有大略。

translations.literal: Yet Chongtao gave his full loyalty to the state and had great strategic vision.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chongtao gave his full loyalty to the state and had great strategic vision.

sentences.zh: 其已破蜀，因遣使者以唐威德風諭南詔諸蠻，欲因以綏來之，可謂有誌矣！

translations.literal: After he had broken Shu he dispatched envoys to proclaim Tang’s majesty and virtue to the Nan Zhao tribes, intending to win them over by gentle persuasion—one may say he had ambition!
translations.idiomatic: After he broke Shu he sent envoys to proclaim Tang’s majesty and virtue to the Nan Zhao tribes, hoping to win them over by gentle persuasion—one may say he had ambition!

sentences.zh: 安重誨

translations.literal: An Chonghui
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui

sentences.zh: 重誨自為中門使，已見親信，而以佐命功臣，處機密之任，事無大小，皆以參決，其勢傾動天下。

translations.literal: From the time Chonghui became director of the Inner Gate he enjoyed the emperor’s trust; as a founding merit minister holding confidential posts, he deliberated on matters great and small, and his power shook the empire.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Chonghui became director of the Inner Gate he enjoyed the emperor’s trust. As a founding merit minister in confidential posts, he weighed every matter great and small, and his power shook the empire.

sentences.zh: 雖其盡忠勞心，時有補益，而恃功矜寵，威福自出，旁無賢人君子之助，其獨見之慮，禍釁所生，至於臣主俱傷，幾滅其族，斯其可哀者也。

translations.literal: Though he labored with loyal heart and sometimes did good, he leaned on merit and favored status, wielded reward and punishment by his own will, had no wise and upright men at his side, and from his solitary counsel sprang disaster—so that ruler and minister both suffered and his clan nearly perished; this is the pity of it.
translations.idiomatic: Though he labored loyally and sometimes did good, he leaned on merit and favored status, wielded reward and punishment as he pleased, had no wise men at his side, and from his solitary counsel sprang disaster—ruler and minister both suffered and his clan nearly perished. That is the pity of it.

sentences.zh: 重誨嘗出，過御史臺門，殿直馬延誤沖其前導，重誨怒，即臺門斬延而後奏。

translations.literal: Once when Chonghui went out he passed the Censorate gate; the palace attendant Ma Yan accidentally blocked his escort; Chonghui in rage cut Yan down at the gate and only afterward reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Chonghui went out he passed the Censorate gate. The palace attendant Ma Yan accidentally blocked his escort; Chonghui in rage cut Yan down at the gate and only afterward reported it.

sentences.zh: 是時，隨駕廳子軍士桑弘遷，毆傷相州錄事參軍；

translations.literal: At that time the bodyguard officer Sang Hongqian beat the magistrate of Xiangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: At that time the bodyguard officer Sang Hongqian beat the magistrate of Xiangzhou;

sentences.zh: 親從兵馬使安虔，走馬沖宰相前導。

translations.literal: the personal attendant An Qian rode at full gallop through the grand councilor’s escort.
translations.idiomatic: the personal attendant An Qian rode at full gallop through the grand councilor’s escort.

sentences.zh: 弘遷罪死，虔決杖而已。

translations.literal: Hongqian was sentenced to death; Qian received flogging only.
translations.idiomatic: Hongqian was sentenced to death; Qian received flogging only.

sentences.zh: 重誨以斬延，乃請降敕處分，明宗不得已從之，由是御史、諫官無敢言者。

translations.literal: Because Chonghui had beheaded Yan he asked that an edict be issued to judge the case; Mingzong unwillingly consented, and from then on censors and remonstrating officials dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Because Chonghui had beheaded Yan he asked for an edict to settle the matter; Mingzong unwillingly consented, and from then on censors and remonstrating officials dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 宰相任圜判三司，以其職事與重誨爭，不能得，圜怒，辭疾，退居於磁州。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Ren Huan ran the Three Departments and quarreled with Chonghui over their duties without prevailing; Huan in anger pleaded illness and retired to Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Ren Huan ran the Three Departments and quarreled with Chonghui over their duties without prevailing. Huan in anger pleaded illness and retired to Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 朱守殷以汴州反，重誨遣人矯詔馳至其家，殺圜而後白，誣圜與守殷通謀，明宗皆不能詰也。

translations.literal: When Zhu Shouyin rebelled at Bianzhou, Chonghui sent men with a forged edict racing to Huan’s home, killed him, and only then reported it—falsely charging Huan with plotting with Shouyin; Mingzong could not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Shouyin rebelled at Bianzhou, Chonghui sent men with a forged edict racing to Huan’s home, killed him, and only then reported it—falsely charging Huan with plotting with Shouyin. Mingzong could not investigate.

sentences.zh: 而重誨恐天下議己因取三司積欠二百餘萬，請放之，冀以悅人而塞責，明宗不得已，為下詔蠲除之。

translations.literal: Yet Chonghui feared public criticism and took two million-odd in Three Department arrears and asked that they be forgiven, hoping to buy men’s favor and stifle censure; Mingzong unwillingly issued an edict remitting them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chonghui feared public criticism and took more than two million in Three Department arrears and asked that they be forgiven, hoping to buy favor and stifle censure. Mingzong unwillingly issued an edict remitting them.

sentences.zh: 其威福自出，多此類也。

translations.literal: His wielding of reward and punishment by his own will was largely of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His wielding of reward and punishment as he pleased was largely of this sort.

sentences.zh: 是時，四方奏事，皆先白重誨然後聞。

translations.literal: At that time memorials from the four quarters all went first to Chonghui before reaching the throne.
translations.idiomatic: At that time memorials from the four quarters all went first to Chonghui before reaching the throne.

sentences.zh: 河南縣獻嘉禾，一莖五穗，重誨視之曰：「偽也。

translations.literal: Henan county presented an auspicious grain stalk with five ears on one stem; Chonghui looked at it and said: “A forgery.
translations.idiomatic: Henan county presented an auspicious grain stalk with five ears on one stem. Chonghui looked at it and said: “A forgery.

sentences.zh: 」笞其人而遣之。

translations.literal: ” He flogged the man and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: ” He flogged the man and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 夏州李仁福進白鷹，重誨卻之，明日，白曰：「陛下詔天下毋得獻鷹鷂，而仁福違詔獻鷹，臣已卻之矣。

translations.literal: Li Renfu of Xias prefecture presented a white hawk; Chonghui refused it; the next day he reported to the throne: “Your Majesty has decreed that none under heaven may present hawks and falcons, yet Renfu defied the decree and presented a hawk; your servant has already refused it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Renfu of Xias prefecture presented a white hawk; Chonghui refused it. The next day he reported: “Your Majesty has decreed that none under heaven may present hawks and falcons, yet Renfu defied the decree and presented a hawk; your servant has already refused it.

sentences.zh: 」重誨出，明宗陰遣人取之以入。

translations.literal: After Chonghui left, Mingzong secretly sent men to fetch it in.
translations.idiomatic: After Chonghui left, Mingzong secretly sent men to fetch it in.

sentences.zh: 佗日，按鷹於西郊，戒左右：「無使重誨知也！

translations.literal: Another day he flew the hawk in the western suburbs, warning those around him: “Do not let Chonghui know!
translations.idiomatic: Another day he flew the hawk in the western suburbs and warned those around him: “Do not let Chonghui know!

sentences.zh: 」宿州進白兔，重誨曰：「兔陰且狡，雖白何為！

translations.literal: Suzhou presented a white rabbit; Chonghui said: “Rabbits are yin creatures and cunning—what good is a white one!
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou presented a white rabbit. Chonghui said: “Rabbits are yin creatures and cunning—what good is a white one!

sentences.zh: 」遂卻而不白。

translations.literal: ” He refused it and did not report it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: ” He refused it and did not report it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 明宗為人雖寬厚，然其性夷狄，果於殺人。

translations.literal: Mingzong as a man was broad and generous, yet by nature he was a barbarian tribesman and quick to kill.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong was broad and generous by nature, yet he was a barbarian tribesman at heart and quick to kill.

sentences.zh: 馬牧軍使田令方所牧馬，瘠而多斃，坐劾當死，重誨諫曰：「使天下聞以馬故，殺一軍使，是謂貴畜而賤人。

translations.literal: Tian Lingfang, horse-pasture commissioner, tended horses that were gaunt and many died; impeached, he merited death; Chonghui remonstrated: “If all under heaven hear that for a horse’s sake a commissioner was killed, they will say we value beasts and cheapen men.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingfang, horse-pasture commissioner, tended horses that were gaunt and many died. Impeached, he merited death. Chonghui remonstrated: “If all under heaven hear that for a horse’s sake a commissioner was killed, they will say we value beasts and cheapen men.

sentences.zh: 」令方因得減死。

translations.literal: Lingfang therefore had his sentence reduced from death.
translations.idiomatic: ” Lingfang therefore had his sentence reduced from death.

sentences.zh: 明宗遣回鶻侯三馳傳至其國。

translations.literal: Mingzong sent the Uighur envoy Hou San post-haste to his country.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong sent the Uighur envoy Hou San post-haste to his country.

sentences.zh: 侯三至醴泉縣，縣素僻，無驛馬，其令劉知章出獵，不時給馬，侯三遽以聞。

translations.literal: When Hou San reached Liquan county—a place always remote with no relay horses—the magistrate Liu Zhizhang had gone hunting and did not supply horses in time; Hou San immediately reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou San reached Liquan county—a place always remote with no relay horses—the magistrate Liu Zhizhang had gone hunting and did not supply horses in time. Hou San immediately reported it.

sentences.zh: 明宗大怒，械知章至京師，將殺之，重誨從容為言，知章乃得不死。

translations.literal: Mingzong in great rage had Zhizhang shackled and brought to the capital to be killed; Chonghui spoke calmly on his behalf and Zhizhang was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong in great rage had Zhizhang shackled and brought to the capital to be killed. Chonghui spoke calmly on his behalf and Zhizhang was spared.

sentences.zh: 其盡忠補益，亦此類也。

translations.literal: His loyal service doing good was also largely of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His loyal service doing good was also largely of this sort.

sentences.zh: 重誨既以天下為己任，遂欲內為社稷之計，而外制諸侯之強。

translations.literal: Once Chonghui took all under heaven as his charge, he wished within to plan for the state’s welfare and without to check powerful feudatories.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chonghui took all under heaven as his charge, he wished within to plan for the state’s welfare and without to check powerful feudatories.

sentences.zh: 然其輕信韓玫之譖，而絕錢镠之臣；

translations.literal: Yet he lightly believed Han Mei’s slanders and cut off Qian Liu’s submission;
translations.idiomatic: Yet he lightly believed Han Mei’s slanders and cut off Qian Liu’s submission;

sentences.zh: 徒陷彥溫於死，而不能去潞王之患；

translations.literal: he only trapped Yanwen in death and could not remove the trouble of the Prince of Lu;
translations.idiomatic: he only trapped Yanwen in death and could not remove the trouble of the Prince of Lu;

sentences.zh: 李嚴一出而知祥貳，仁矩未至而董璋叛；

translations.literal: Li Yan went out once and Zhixiang turned disloyal; Renju had not arrived and Dong Zhang rebelled;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan went out once and Zhixiang turned disloyal; Renju had not arrived and Dong Zhang rebelled;

sentences.zh: 四方騷動，師旅並興，如投膏止火，適足速之。

translations.literal: the four quarters rose in alarm, armies marched everywhere—as if tossing grease on fire, only hastening the blaze.
translations.idiomatic: the four quarters rose in alarm and armies marched everywhere—as if tossing grease on fire, only hastening the blaze.

sentences.zh: 此所謂獨見之慮，禍釁所生也。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by “from solitary counsel sprang disaster.”
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by “from solitary counsel sprang disaster.”

sentences.zh: 錢镠據有兩浙，號兼吳越而王，自梁及莊宗，常異其禮，以羈縻臣屬之而已。

translations.literal: Qian Liu held the two Zhe provinces, styled king of Wu and Yue combined; from Liang through Zhuangzong the court had always treated his rites differently, restraining him as a subject only.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu held the two Zhe provinces and styled himself king of Wu and Yue combined. From Liang through Zhuangzong the court had always treated his rites differently, restraining him as a subject only.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，镠遣使朝京師，寓書重誨，其禮慢。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne Liu sent envoys to court and wrote to Chonghui in disrespectful terms.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne Liu sent envoys to court and wrote to Chonghui in disrespectful terms.

sentences.zh: 重誨怒，未有以發，乃遣其嬖吏韓玫、副供奉官烏昭遇復使於镠。

translations.literal: Chonghui raged but had no opening; he sent his favorite clerk Han Mei and deputy palace attendant Wu Zhaoyu again as envoys to Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui raged but had no opening. He sent his favorite clerk Han Mei and deputy palace attendant Wu Zhaoyu again as envoys to Liu.

sentences.zh: 而玫恃重誨勢，數淩辱昭遇，因醉使酒，以馬箠擊之。

translations.literal: Mei relied on Chonghui’s power, repeatedly insulted Zhaoyu, and when drunk ordered wine and struck him with a riding crop.
translations.idiomatic: Mei relied on Chonghui’s power, repeatedly insulted Zhaoyu, and when drunk ordered wine and struck him with a riding crop.

sentences.zh: 镠欲奏其事，昭遇以為辱國，固止之。

translations.literal: Liu wished to memorialize the affair; Zhaoyu thought it would shame the state and firmly stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu wished to memorialize the affair; Zhaoyu thought it would shame the state and firmly stopped him.

sentences.zh: 及玫還，返譖於重誨曰：「昭遇見镠，舞蹈稱臣，而以朝廷事私告镠。

translations.literal: When Mei returned he slandered Zhaoyu to Chonghui: “Zhaoyu saw Liu, bowed in dance and called himself subject, and privately told Liu court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Mei returned he slandered Zhaoyu to Chonghui: “Zhaoyu saw Liu, bowed in dance and called himself subject, and privately told Liu court affairs.

sentences.zh: 」昭遇坐死御史獄，乃下制削奪镠官爵，以太師致仕，於是錢氏遂絕於唐矣。

translations.literal: Zhaoyu died in the censorate prison; an edict then stripped Liu of rank and title and retired him as Grand Preceptor—thus the Qian house was severed from Tang.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhaoyu died in the censorate prison. An edict then stripped Liu of rank and title and retired him as Grand Preceptor—thus the Qian house was severed from Tang.

sentences.zh: 潞王從珂為河中節度使，重誨以謂從珂非李氏子，後必為國家患，乃欲陰圖之。

translations.literal: Prince of Lu Congke was military governor of Hezhong; Chonghui judged that Congke was not a Li clansman and would surely endanger the state, and wished secretly to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Lu Congke was military governor of Hezhong. Chonghui judged that Congke was not a Li clansman and would surely endanger the state, and wished secretly to plot against him.

sentences.zh: 從珂閱馬黃龍莊，其牙內指揮使楊彥溫閉城以叛。

translations.literal: Congke was reviewing horses at Huanglong Manor; his garrison commander Yang Yanwen shut the city and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Congke was reviewing horses at Huanglong Manor when his garrison commander Yang Yanwen shut the city and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 從珂遣人謂彥溫曰：「我遇汝厚，何苦而反邪？

translations.literal: Congke sent word to Yanwen: “I treated you generously—why rebel?
translations.idiomatic: Congke sent word to Yanwen: “I treated you generously—why rebel?

sentences.zh: 」報曰：「彥溫非叛也，得樞密院宣，請公趨歸朝廷耳！

translations.literal: The reply: “Yanwen is no rebel; I received an edict from the Bureau of Military Affairs ordering you to hurry back to court!
translations.idiomatic: The reply: “Yanwen is no rebel. I received an edict from the Bureau of Military Affairs ordering you to hurry back to court!

sentences.zh: 」從珂走虞鄉，馳騎上變。

translations.literal: Congke fled to Yu village and sent riders to report the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: ” Congke fled to Yu village and sent riders to report the crisis.

sentences.zh: 明宗疑其事不明，欲究其所以，乃遣殿直都知範氳以金帶襲衣、金鞍勒馬賜彥溫，拜彥溫絳州刺史，以誘致之。

translations.literal: Mingzong doubted the affair was unclear and wished to get to the bottom of it; he sent the palace attendant Fan Hun with a gold belt, surcoat, gold saddle, and bridle as gifts to Yanwen and made Yanwen prefect of Jiangzhou to lure him in.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong doubted the affair was unclear and wished to get to the bottom of it. He sent the palace attendant Fan Hun with a gold belt, surcoat, gold saddle, and bridle as gifts to Yanwen and made Yanwen prefect of Jiangzhou to lure him in.

sentences.zh: 重誨固請用兵，明宗不得已，乃遣侍衛指揮使藥彥稠、西京留守索自通率兵討之，而誡曰：「為我生致彥溫，吾將自訊其事。

translations.literal: Chonghui firmly pressed for military action; Mingzong unwillingly sent Palace Guard commander Yao Yanzhou and western capital intendant Suo Zitong with troops to punish him, charging them: “Bring Yanwen to me alive—I will question him myself.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui firmly pressed for military action. Mingzong unwillingly sent Palace Guard commander Yao Yanzhou and western capital intendant Suo Zitong with troops to punish him, charging them: “Bring Yanwen to me alive—I will question him myself.

sentences.zh: 」彥稠等攻破河中，希重誨旨，斬彥溫以滅口。

translations.literal: Yanzhou and the others broke Hezhong, hoping to please Chonghui, and beheaded Yanwen to silence him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yanzhou and the others broke Hezhong, hoping to please Chonghui, and beheaded Yanwen to silence him.

sentences.zh: 重誨率群臣稱賀，明宗大怒曰：「朕家事不了，卿等不合致賀！

translations.literal: Chonghui led the ministers in congratulation; Mingzong raged: “I cannot even settle my own household affairs—you must not congratulate!
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui led the ministers in congratulation. Mingzong raged: “I cannot even settle my own household affairs—you must not congratulate!

sentences.zh: 」從珂罷鎮，居清化裏第。

translations.literal: Congke was removed from his post and lived at his Qinghua Lane mansion.
translations.idiomatic: ” Congke was removed from his post and lived at his Qinghua Lane mansion.

sentences.zh: 重誨數諷宰相，言從珂失守，宜得罪，馮道因白請行法。

translations.literal: Chonghui repeatedly hinted to the grand councilors that Congke had failed in his defense and deserved punishment; Feng Dao reported asking that the law be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui repeatedly hinted to the grand councilors that Congke had failed in his defense and deserved punishment. Feng Dao reported asking that the law be applied.

sentences.zh: 明宗怒曰：「吾兒為奸人所中，事未辨明，公等出此言，是不欲容吾兒人間邪？

translations.literal: Mingzong raged: “My son was struck by villains and the matter is not yet clear—will you speak this way? Do you not wish my son to live among men?
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong raged: “My son was struck by villains and the matter is not yet clear—will you speak this way? Do you not wish my son to live among men?

sentences.zh: 」趙鳳因言：「《春秋》責帥之義，所以勵為臣者。

translations.literal: Zhao Feng then said: “The Spring and Autumn holds the commander accountable—this is to encourage subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng then said: “The Spring and Autumn Annals holds the commander accountable—this is to encourage subjects.

sentences.zh: 」明宗曰：「皆非公等意也！

translations.literal: Mingzong said: “None of this is your own thought!
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong said: “None of this is your own thought!

sentences.zh: 」道等惶恐而退。

translations.literal: Dao and the others withdrew in fear.
translations.idiomatic: ” Dao and the others withdrew in fear.

sentences.zh: 居數日，道等又以為請，明宗顧左右而言他。

translations.literal: After several days Dao and the others asked again; Mingzong looked to those around him and changed the subject.
translations.idiomatic: After several days Dao and the others asked again. Mingzong looked to those around him and changed the subject.

sentences.zh: 明日，重誨乃自論列，明宗曰：「公欲如何處置，我即從公！

translations.literal: The next day Chonghui argued the matter himself; Mingzong said: “However you wish to dispose of it, I will follow you!
translations.idiomatic: The next day Chonghui argued the matter himself. Mingzong said: “However you wish to dispose of it, I will follow you!

sentences.zh: 」重誨曰：「此父子之際，非臣所宜言，惟陛下裁之。

translations.literal: Chonghui said: “This is a matter between father and son—not something your servant should discuss; let Your Majesty decide.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui said: “This is a matter between father and son—not something your servant should discuss. Let Your Majesty decide.

sentences.zh: 」明宗曰：「吾為小校時，衣食不能自足，此兒為我擔石灰，拾馬糞，以相養活，今貴為天子，獨不能庇之邪！

translations.literal: Mingzong said: “When I was a petty officer I could not feed myself; this boy carried lime and gathered horse dung to keep me alive—now he is exalted as Son of Heaven, and I cannot shelter him?
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong said: “When I was a petty officer I could not feed myself. This boy carried lime and gathered horse dung to keep me alive—now he is exalted as Son of Heaven, and I cannot shelter him?

sentences.zh: 使其杜門私第，亦何與公事！

translations.literal: Let him keep his doors shut in private quarters—what has that to do with state business!
translations.idiomatic: Let him keep his doors shut in private quarters—what has that to do with state business!

sentences.zh: 」重誨由是不復敢言。

translations.literal: From then Chonghui no longer dared speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: ” From then Chonghui no longer dared speak of it.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥鎮西川，董璋鎮東川，二人皆有異志，重誨每事裁抑，務欲制其奸心，凡兩川守將更代，多用己所親信，必以精兵從之，漸令分戍諸州，以虞緩急。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang governed Xichuan and Dong Zhang governed Dongchuan; both harbored disloyal intentions; Chonghui on every matter checked and suppressed them, striving to control their treacherous hearts; whenever commanders in the two circuits were replaced he mostly used men of his own trust and always sent crack troops with them, gradually posting them to garrison various prefectures against emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang governed Xichuan and Dong Zhang governed Dongchuan; both harbored disloyal intentions. Chonghui checked and suppressed them at every turn, striving to control their treacherous hearts. Whenever commanders in the two circuits were replaced he mostly used men of his own trust and always sent crack troops with them, gradually posting them to garrison various prefectures against emergencies.

sentences.zh: 二人覺之，以為圖己，益不自安。

translations.literal: The two men noticed and thought they were being targeted; they grew still less secure.
translations.idiomatic: The two men noticed and thought they were being targeted; they grew still less secure.

sentences.zh: 既而遣李嚴為西川監軍，知祥大怒，斬嚴；

translations.literal: Later Li Yan was sent as army supervisor of Xichuan; Zhixiang in fury beheaded Yan;
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Yan was sent as army supervisor of Xichuan; Zhixiang in fury beheaded Yan.

sentences.zh: 又分閬州為保寧軍，以李仁矩為節度使以制璋，且削其地，璋以兵攻殺仁矩。

translations.literal: Langzhou was split off as Baoning army with Li Renju as military governor to check Zhang—and his territory was reduced; Zhang attacked with troops and killed Renju.
translations.idiomatic: Langzhou was split off as the Baoning army with Li Renju as military governor to check Zhang—and Zhang’s territory was reduced. Zhang attacked with troops and killed Renju.

sentences.zh: 二人遂皆反。

translations.literal: Both men then rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Both men then rebelled.

sentences.zh: 唐兵戍蜀者，積三萬人，其後知祥殺璋，兼據兩川，而唐之精兵皆陷蜀。

translations.literal: Tang troops garrisoned in Shu totaled thirty thousand men; afterward Zhixiang killed Zhang and held both circuits together, and Tang’s finest troops were all trapped in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang troops garrisoned in Shu totaled thirty thousand men. Later Zhixiang killed Zhang and held both circuits together, and Tang’s finest troops were all trapped in Shu.

sentences.zh: 初，明宗幸汴州，重誨建議，欲因以伐吳，而明宗難之。

translations.literal: Earlier when Mingzong visited Bianzhou, Chonghui proposed using the occasion to attack Wu, but Mingzong found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier when Mingzong visited Bianzhou, Chonghui proposed using the occasion to attack Wu, but Mingzong hesitated.

sentences.zh: 其後戶部尚書李鏻得吳諜者言：「徐知誥欲舉吳國以稱藩，願得安公一言以為信。

translations.literal: After that Li Lin, Minister of Revenue, obtained a Wu spy who said: “Xu Zhigao wishes to submit the Wu state as a vassal and hopes to receive a word from Lord An as pledge.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Lin, Minister of Revenue, took a Wu spy who said Xu Zhigao meant to bring Wu under the throne as a vassal state—if only Lord An would give his word as pledge.

sentences.zh: 」鏻即引諜者見重誨，重誨大喜以為然，乃以玉帶與諜者，使遺知誥為信，其直千緡。

translations.literal: ” Li Lin at once brought the spy to Chonghui; Chonghui was greatly pleased and believed it; he gave the spy a jade belt to send to Zhigao as pledge—worth a thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lin brought the man straight to Chonghui. Chonghui was delighted and took it for truth; he gave the spy a jade belt to carry to Zhigao as token—worth a thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 初不以其事聞，其後逾年，知誥之問不至，始奏貶鏻行軍司馬。

translations.literal: At first he did not report the matter; more than a year later, when no word came from Zhigao, he only then memorialized to demote Li Lin to marching army adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: He never reported it at first. More than a year passed with no word from Zhigao; only then did he memorialize to demote Li Lin to marching army adjutant.

sentences.zh: 已而捧聖都軍使李行德、十將張儉告變，言：「樞密承旨李虔徽語其客邊彥溫云：『重誨私募士卒，繕治甲器，欲自伐吳。

translations.literal: Before long Li Xingde, commander of the Baosheng Capital Garrison, and tenth-rank officer Zhang Jian reported a mutiny, saying: “Privy Council chief clerk Li Qianhui told his guest Bian Yanzheng: ‘Chonghui is secretly recruiting soldiers and repairing armor; he means to campaign against Wu on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Xingde, commander of the Baosheng Capital Garrison, and tenth-rank officer Zhang Jian reported treason: Privy Council chief clerk Li Qianhui had told his guest Bian Yanzheng that Chonghui was secretly raising troops and forging arms to march on Wu by himself.

sentences.zh: 又與諜者交私。

translations.literal: He also keeps private dealings with spies.’
translations.idiomatic: He was also in private league with spies.’

sentences.zh: 』」明宗以問重誨，重誨惶恐，請究其事。

translations.literal: ” Mingzong questioned Chonghui; Chonghui was terrified and asked that the matter be investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong questioned Chonghui. Chonghui was terrified and begged for a full inquiry.

sentences.zh: 明宗初頗疑之，大臣左右皆為之辨，既而少解，始告重誨以彥溫之言，因廷詰彥溫，具伏其詐，於是君臣相顧泣下。

translations.literal: At first Mingzong was quite suspicious; ministers and attendants all argued in Chonghui’s defense; after a little he relented, then told Chonghui Bian’s words and questioned Bian in court—Bian fully confessed his fraud; ruler and minister looked at each other and wept.
translations.idiomatic: At first Mingzong was deeply suspicious; ministers and attendants all spoke for Chonghui. After a time he softened, told Chonghui what Bian had said, and questioned Bian in open court. Bian confessed the whole fraud. Ruler and minister looked at each other and wept.

sentences.zh: 彥溫、行德、儉皆坐族誅。

translations.literal: Bian Yanzheng, Li Xingde, and Zhang Jian were all executed along with their clans.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Yanzheng, Li Xingde, and Zhang Jian were all executed, their clans with them.

sentences.zh: 重誨因求解職，明宗慰之曰：「事已辨，慎無措之胸中。

translations.literal: Chonghui then asked to resign; Mingzong comforted him: “The matter is cleared—be careful not to store it in your breast.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui asked to resign. Mingzong comforted him: “It is settled—do not carry it in your heart.

sentences.zh: 」重誨論請不已，明宗怒曰：「放卿去，朕不患無人！

translations.literal: ” Chonghui pressed his plea without end; Mingzong angrily said: “Go if you like—I am not short of men!
translations.idiomatic: ” Chonghui would not stop pleading. Mingzong snapped: “Go then—I am not short of men!

sentences.zh: 」顧武德使孟漢瓊至中書，趣馮道等議代重誨者。

translations.literal: ” He turned to Wude commissioner Meng Hanqiong and sent him to the Secretariat to urge Feng Dao and the others to discuss a replacement for Chonghui.
translations.idiomatic: ” He turned to Wude commissioner Meng Hanqiong and sent him to the Secretariat to hurry Feng Dao and the rest into choosing a successor.

sentences.zh: 馮道曰：「諸公茍惜安公，使得罷去，是紓其禍也。

translations.literal: Feng Dao said: “If you gentlemen cherish Lord An, let him be dismissed—that will ease his peril.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao said: “If you truly mean to save Lord An, let him go—that is how you spare him worse harm.

sentences.zh: 」趙鳳以為大臣不可輕動。

translations.literal: ” Zhao Feng held that a great minister must not be lightly moved.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhao Feng argued that a chief minister must not be lightly displaced.

sentences.zh: 遂以範延光為樞密使，而重誨居職如故。

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang was then made privy commissioner, but Chonghui remained in office as before.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang was made privy commissioner, but Chonghui kept his post as before.

sentences.zh: 董璋等反，遣石敬瑭討之，而川路險阻，糧運甚艱，每費一石，而致一斗。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhang and others rebelled, Shi Jingtang was sent to suppress them; but Sichuan routes were steep and perilous and grain transport extremely hard—each shi spent yielded only one dou delivered.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhang and others rebelled, Shi Jingtang was sent to suppress them. The Sichuan roads were steep and perilous; grain transport was agony—each shi spent bought barely a dou delivered.

sentences.zh: 自關以西，民苦輸送，往往亡聚山林為盜賊。

translations.literal: West of the Pass, the people were worn out by transport duties and often fled into hills and forests to band together as robbers.
translations.idiomatic: West of the Pass the people were broken by transport labor; many fled into the hills and turned bandit.

sentences.zh: 明宗謂重誨曰：「事勢如此，吾當自行。

translations.literal: Mingzong said to Chonghui: “Matters stand thus—I ought to go myself.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong told Chonghui: “Things have come to this—I should go myself.

sentences.zh: 」重誨曰：「此臣之責也。

translations.literal: ” Chonghui said: “That is this subject’s duty.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chonghui said: “That is my duty.

sentences.zh: 」乃請行。

translations.literal: ” He then asked to go.
translations.idiomatic: ” And he asked to go.

sentences.zh: 關西之人聞重誨來，皆已恐動，而重誨日馳數百里，遠近驚駭。

translations.literal: People west of the Pass heard Chonghui was coming and were already shaken with fear; Chonghui raced several hundred li each day—the region far and near was stricken with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: West of the Pass, word that Chonghui was coming already had people trembling. He drove several hundred li a day; far and near the land shook with fear.

sentences.zh: 督趣糧運，日夜不絕，斃踣道路者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: He drove grain transport night and day without cease; corpses collapsed on the roads beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He drove grain convoys day and night without pause; the dead littered the roads beyond count.

sentences.zh: 重誨過鳳翔，節度使朱弘昭延之寢室，使其妻子奉事左右甚謹。

translations.literal: Chonghui passed through Fengxiang; military governor Zhu Hongzhao received him in his private chamber and had his wife and children wait on him with great care.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengxiang, military governor Zhu Hongzhao brought him into his private chamber and had wife and children attend him with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 重誨酒酣，為弘昭言：「昨被讒構，幾不自全，賴人主明聖，得保家族。

translations.literal: Chonghui, well drunk, told Hongzhao: “Yesterday I was slandered and nearly destroyed; by the lord’s wisdom and sagacity I kept my family safe.
translations.idiomatic: Well drunk, Chonghui told Hongzhao: “I was slandered yesterday and nearly lost everything. Only the sovereign’s wisdom saved my house.

sentences.zh: 」因感嘆泣下。

translations.literal: ” He sighed in emotion and wept.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sighed and wept.

sentences.zh: 重誨去，弘昭馳騎上言：「重誨怨望，不可令至行營，恐其生事。

translations.literal: After Chonghui left, Hongzhao galloped ahead with a memorial: “Chonghui bears resentment; he must not be allowed to reach the field camp—I fear he may make trouble.
translations.idiomatic: After Chonghui left, Hongzhao galloped ahead with a memorial: “Chonghui is full of grievance. Do not let him reach the field camp—he may make trouble.

sentences.zh: 」而宣徽使孟漢瓊自行營使還，亦言西人震駭之狀，因述重誨過惡。

translations.literal: Privy Treasury commissioner Meng Hanqiong also returned from the field-camp commissioner post and spoke of how the western people were shaken with terror—and related Chonghui’s faults.
translations.idiomatic: Privy Treasury commissioner Meng Hanqiong had just returned from the field camp and told of the terror in the west—and listed Chonghui’s crimes.

sentences.zh: 重誨行至三泉，被召還。

translations.literal: Chonghui reached Sanquan and was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui reached Sanquan and was recalled.

sentences.zh: 過鳳翔，弘昭拒而不納，重誨懼，馳趨京師。

translations.literal: Passing Fengxiang again, Hongzhao refused him entry; Chonghui was afraid and raced toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Fengxiang again, Hongzhao shut his gates. Chonghui was terrified and raced for the capital.

sentences.zh: 未至，拜河中節度使。

translations.literal: Before he arrived he was appointed military governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived he was named military governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 重誨已罷，希旨者爭求其過。

translations.literal: Once Chonghui had lost office, those seeking favor competed to find his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chonghui fell, men eager to please hunted his faults.

sentences.zh: 宦者安希倫，坐與重誨交私，常與重誨陰伺宮中動息，事發棄市。

translations.literal: The eunuch An Xilun, charged with private dealings with Chonghui and often spying on palace movements with him in secret, was executed in the marketplace when the affair came out.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch An Xilun, who had kept private dealings with Chonghui and often watched palace movements with him in secret, was executed in the marketplace when the affair broke.

sentences.zh: 重誨益懼，因上章告老。

translations.literal: Chonghui grew only more afraid and submitted a memorial to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui grew only more afraid and memorialized to retire.

sentences.zh: 以太子太師致仕；

translations.literal: He was retired as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent;
translations.idiomatic: He was retired as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent;

sentences.zh: 而以李從璋為河中節度使，遣藥彥稠率兵如河中虞變。

translations.literal: Li Congzhang was made military governor of Hezhong, and Yao Yanchou was sent with troops to Hezhong to guard against trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Li Congzhang was made military governor of Hezhong, and Yao Yanchou was sent with troops to watch for trouble.

sentences.zh: 重誨子崇緒、崇贊，宿衛京師，聞制下，即日奔其父。

translations.literal: Chonghui’s sons Chongxu and Chongzan, on palace guard duty in the capital, heard the edict issue and that same day fled to their father.
