translations.idiomatic: Chonghui’s sons Chongxu and Chongzan, on palace guard in the capital, heard the edict and fled to their father that same day.

sentences.zh: 重誨見之，驚曰：「渠安得來！

translations.literal: Chonghui saw them and cried in alarm: “How did they come here!
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui saw them and cried: “How did they get here!

sentences.zh: 」已而曰：「此非渠意，為人所使耳。

translations.literal: ” Then he said: “This was not their own intent—they were sent by others.
translations.idiomatic: ” Then he said: “This was not their doing—they were sent by others.

sentences.zh: 吾以一死報國，余復何言！

translations.literal: I will repay the state with one death—what else is there to say!
translations.idiomatic: I owe the state one death—what more is there to say!

sentences.zh: 」乃械送二子於京師，行至陜州，下獄。

translations.literal: ” He had both sons shackled and sent to the capital; reaching Shan prefecture they were thrown in prison.
translations.idiomatic: ” He shackled both sons and sent them to the capital. At Shan prefecture they were thrown in prison.

sentences.zh: 明宗又遣翟光業至河中，視重誨去就，戒曰：「有異志，則與從璋圖之。

translations.literal: Mingzong also sent Zhai Guangye to Hezhong to watch Chonghui’s intentions, instructing him: “If he has different designs, work with Congzhang to deal with him.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong also sent Zhai Guangye to Hezhong to watch Chonghui’s intent, telling him: “If he shows disloyalty, work with Congzhang to dispose of him.

sentences.zh: 」又遣宦者使於重誨。

translations.literal: ” He also sent a eunuch envoy to Chonghui.
translations.idiomatic: ” He also sent a eunuch envoy to Chonghui.

sentences.zh: 使者見重誨，號泣不已，重誨問其故，使者曰：「人言公有異志，朝廷遣藥彥稠率師至矣！

translations.literal: The envoy saw Chonghui and wept without end; Chonghui asked why; the envoy said: “People say you have different designs—the court has sent Yao Yanchou with an army!
translations.idiomatic: The envoy saw Chonghui and wept without stopping. Chonghui asked why. The envoy said: “Men say you mean rebellion—the court has sent Yao Yanchou with an army!

sentences.zh: 」重誨曰：「吾死未塞責，遽勞朝廷興師，以重明主之憂。

translations.literal: ” Chonghui said: “My death has not yet covered my guilt—yet suddenly the court must raise troops, adding to our enlightened lord’s cares.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chonghui said: “I have not yet paid my debt with death—and already the court must raise troops and burden our lord with fresh grief.

sentences.zh: 」光業至，從璋率兵圍重誨第，入拜於庭。

translations.literal: ” Guangye arrived; Congzhang led troops to surround Chonghui’s mansion and entered to bow in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: ” When Guangye arrived, Congzhang led troops to surround Chonghui’s mansion and entered to bow in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 重誨降而答拜，從璋以楇擊其首，重誨妻走抱之而呼曰：「令公死未晚，何遽如此！

translations.literal: Chonghui descended to return the bow; Congzhang struck his head with a club; Chonghui’s wife ran to embrace him and cried: “My lord’s death is not yet due—why so hurried!
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui came down to return the bow. Congzhang struck his head with a club. Chonghui’s wife ran to embrace him and cried: “My lord need not die yet—why so hurried!

sentences.zh: 」又擊其首，夫妻皆死，流血盈庭。

translations.literal: ” He struck his head again; husband and wife both died; blood filled the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: ” He struck again. Husband and wife both died; blood filled the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 從璋檢責其家貲，不及數千緡而已。

translations.literal: Congzhang searched his household property—it amounted to less than a few thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhang searched his household goods—they came to less than a few thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 明宗下詔，以其絕錢镠，致孟知祥、董璋反，及議伐吳，以為罪。

translations.literal: Mingzong issued an edict listing as his crimes cutting off Qian Liu, causing Meng Zhixiang and Dong Zhang to rebel, and proposing to campaign against Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong issued an edict naming his crimes: severing ties with Qian Liu, provoking Meng Zhixiang and Dong Zhang to rebel, and urging war on Wu.

sentences.zh: 並殺其二子，其餘子孫皆免。

translations.literal: Both sons were also killed; the rest of his descendants were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Both sons were killed as well; the rest of his line were spared.

sentences.zh: 重誨得罪，知其必死，嘆曰：「我固當死，但恨不與國家除去潞王！

translations.literal: When Chonghui fell from grace and knew he must die, he sighed: “I ought to die—but I regret not removing the Prince of Lu for the state!
translations.idiomatic: When Chonghui knew he must die, he sighed: “I deserve death—but I regret not clearing the Prince of Lu away for the realm!

sentences.zh: 」此其恨也。

translations.literal: That was his grievance.
translations.idiomatic: That was his grievance.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，官失其職久矣！

translations.literal: Alas—the offices have long lost their proper duties!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—the offices have long lost their proper duties!

sentences.zh: 予讀梁宣底，見敬翔、李振為崇政院使，凡承上之旨，宣之宰相而奉行之。

translations.literal: Reading the Liang State Foundation Records, I see Jing Xiang and Li Zhen as Chongzheng Court commissioners: whatever they received of the sovereign’s will they announced to the chancellors, who carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the Liang State Foundation Records, I find Jing Xiang and Li Zhen as Chongzheng Court commissioners: whatever the sovereign commanded, they announced to the chancellors, and the chancellors executed it.

sentences.zh: 宰相有非其見時而事當上決者，與其被旨而有所復請者，則具記事而入，因崇政使聞，得旨則復宣而出之。

translations.literal: If a chancellor had a matter requiring the sovereign’s decision that had not yet been seen, or if, having received a directive, he wished to request reconsideration, he wrote out the matter in full and entered, conveyed it through the Chongzheng commissioner, and once he received the directive, it was announced again and issued.
translations.idiomatic: If a chancellor had business needing the sovereign’s judgment that had not yet been laid before him, or if, having received an order, he wished to ask again, he wrote the matter out in full and entered; the Chongzheng commissioner carried it in; once the sovereign answered, the answer was announced and issued.

sentences.zh: 梁之崇政使，乃唐樞密之職，蓋出納之任也，唐常以宦者為之，至梁戒其禍，始更用士人，其備顧問、參謀議於中則有之，未始專行事於外也。

translations.literal: The Liang Chongzheng commissioner was Tang’s Privy Council post—essentially disbursement and receipt. Tang usually used eunuchs; Liang, heeding the disaster, at last changed to literati. To serve as advisers and discuss policy within the palace—yes—but never to conduct affairs on their own outside.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang Chongzheng commissioner held what had been Tang’s Privy Council post—essentially the channel in and out. Tang usually put eunuchs in it; Liang, warned by the ruin that brought, at last used literati. They might advise and debate within the palace—but never conduct affairs on their own outside it.

sentences.zh: 至崇韜、重誨為之，始復唐樞密之名，然權侔於宰相矣。

translations.literal: When Chongtao and Chonghui held the post they restored Tang’s Privy Council name, yet their power matched the chancellors’.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongtao and Chonghui took the post they restored Tang’s Privy Council name—yet their power matched the chancellors’.

sentences.zh: 從世因之，遂分為二，文事任宰相，武事任樞密。

translations.literal: Congke’s generation continued it; affairs were then split in two—civil matters to the chancellors, military matters to the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: Congke’s generation kept the practice; affairs split in two—civil work to the chancellors, military work to the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 樞密之任既重，而宰相自此失其職也。

translations.literal: Once the Privy Council post grew weighty, the chancellors from that time lost their proper duties.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Privy Council grew heavy, the chancellors from that day lost their proper place.
